title: Midland media library tag record (v4)
description: One record per image in Sales/1. Trailer Photos. `photo` and `path_derived` are populated by code during enumeration. `vision` is the ONLY object a model is ever asked to produce, and it must be produced without being shown `path_derived` -- see docs/routines/02-thursday-iteration.md for why.

photo.description: Populated by the enumeration walk. No model involvement.

path.description: Full path from the library root.

media_class.description: Decided by extension during enumeration, so video never reaches a vision call.

depth.description: Folder depth below the library root. Used to sanity-check that the walk actually recursed.

filename_is_descriptive.description: False for camera defaults (IMG_/DSC/DSCN/P10/timestamp patterns). True filenames are a free validation signal.

shoot_group.description: Stable id for a run of consecutive camera-default filenames within one folder. Shoot-level attributes may propagate across a group; per-frame attributes (shot_type, defects, usability) may NOT.

path_derived.description: Parsed from the folder path. Authoritative -- the path is Midland's own filing decision, and is trusted over anything a model reports. A model is never asked for these.

variant.description: Level-2 folder with any leading "N." stripped, e.g. "Semi Drop Deck Trailers".

axle_config_from_path.description: Only where the path states it. Two axles is Tandem; `bogie` is not a value in this schema.

job_numbers.description: All job numbers named in the path. More than one means the folder holds more than one trailer, so the path cannot say which trailer is in a given frame.

content_expectation.description: Set from the folder, and the reason a frame can be checked against where it is filed. `competitor` marks z. Opposition Trailers.

vision.description: The model's entire output. Every enum admits `unknown`, and where a feature could simply be out of frame, `not_visible` is offered as distinct from `unknown`: use `not_visible` when the feature is confidently outside the frame or occluded, `unknown` when it is in frame but cannot be judged. A model forced to always emit a substantive value will invent one; these two escapes exist so it never has to. Emitting `unknown` is a correct answer and is never penalised.

media_kind.description: What kind of image this is, before anything about its content.

subject_type.description: `partial_view_cropped` is for a frame of a whole trailer where the framing cuts off part of it - common, and not the same as a deliberate component detail.

visible_text.description: Text legible in the frame -- customer signage, branding, VIN plates, chassis-marked job or build numbers, container numbers, compliance plates. Transcribe only what is actually legible; never complete a partially readable string. Container numbers belong to the container, not the trailer, so they can distinguish one unit from another WITHIN a frame but must not be used to link frames or identify a trailer. Registration plates must not be used for identity at all -- see trailers[].identifying_text.

marketing_usability.description: hero = publishable as a lead image; good = usable in collateral; usable = fine as a supporting or record shot; record_only = keep for the record, not for marketing; reject = do not use.

defects.description: Empty array means none observed. Image ORIENTATION is not a defect - rotated files are corrected in the viewer, so tag the content as if it were upright.

notes.description: At most one sentence, and only where it says something the enums cannot. Not a place to restate enum values, and not a place to speculate about specifications, dimensions, part numbers or ratings -- none of those are legible in a photograph. The word `bogie` must not appear.

trailers.description: ONE ENTRY PER TRAILER VISIBLE IN THE FRAME. A frame showing a four-unit road train produces four entries, each tagged on its own merits - never one averaged entry, and never one entry's values copied across the rest. Units differ within a single combination, and a cropped frame may show the axles of one unit and not another, so each entry carries its own axle_count and its own confidence. Empty array where no trailer is present (a document, a bare component, a drawing).

axle_count.description: Count the axles on the trailer only, excluding any prime mover. Midland house vocabulary: two axles is TANDEM. The word `bogie` is not a permitted value anywhere in this schema and must not appear in any free-text field. AN AXLE GROUP DOES NOT BELONG TO THE TRAILER IT APPEARS TO SIT UNDER. In a B-DOUBLE the lead trailer carries a fifth wheel / turntable on a tail section mounted directly above its OWN rear axle group, and the second trailer's kingpin sits on it -- so that group sits beneath the front of the SECOND trailer's body while belonging to the lead one. In an A-DOUBLE / road train the units are joined by a drawbar to a CONVERTER DOLLY which has its own axles and its own fifth wheel, and those axles belong to neither trailer. Assign a group by tracing the chassis rail back to the body it is attached to, never by what is above it. If the chassis cannot be traced, answer not_visible on both units rather than guessing from position. Dog trailers mislead the same way, having a front group under their own front end as well as a rear group. Note the A/B naming is ambiguous -- yard usage calls a B-double's lead trailer the A-trailer, regulator usage reserves A for drawbar-coupled trailers -- so record the physical facts and keep both senses out of the tags.

trailer_configuration.description: 'tag_trailer' HAS BEEN RENAMED to drawbar_plant_trailer: it carries three incompatible meanings, two of them on Midland's own site (their plant trailer product, and the REAR unit of a B-double). Never emit 'tag_trailer'; it is an input alias only. Geometry: pig = one axle group at the CENTRE of the deck; dog = a group at each end, front group steering on a turntable; drawbar_plant_trailer = fixed drawbar, no steering front group. super_dog = single front + tandem rear (3 axles); quad_dog = 5+.

body_type.description: DROP DECK AND STEP DECK ARE THE SAME THING in Australian usage -- Midland state this directly -- so there is no step_deck value; use drop_deck. double_drop_deck has two deck drops with a well between. drop_deck_widener covers what US sources call a lowboy. moving_floor, side_tipper, super_tilt and car_carrier are COMPETITOR bodies Midland do not build, so seeing one is a strong hint the subject is not a Midland product.

rear_ramp.description: BEAVERTAIL AND FIXED ARE EASILY MISTAGGED AS 'none' because neither is a separate ramp-shaped object -- a beavertail is the rear section of the deck itself, angled down. Read the rear deck profile. Stowed bi-fold folds back on itself with a hinge line across the middle; stowed slide-out retracts under the deck and may be nearly invisible.

coaming_type.description: Midland describe coaming four different ways across their site and misspell it 'combing'. 'TFB' is deliberately NOT a value -- it appears once on their site, defined nowhere, so no tagger can be asked to identify it. Ask Midland engineering before adding it.

suspension_mount.description: JOB CARD ONLY -- THE VISION PASS MUST ALWAYS EMIT not_visible. Over-slung/under-slung describes where the leaf spring sits relative to the axle beam. Every source found for these terms is US-origin and about light trailers; Midland never use either word. On an air-bag trailing-arm suspension the distinction is where the axle seat sits on the beam, which is not visible from outside the assembly at all. This is a field a model would guess at, which is exactly what this schema exists to prevent.

coupling_type.description: ball_race_turntable is a low-profile turntable Midland offer as an alternative to a dolly's fifth wheel -- NOT the same as bartlett_ball. Midland spell Ringfeder three ways and misspell Pintle as 'Pintel'; those are input aliases, not values.

is_midland_product.description: Whether the trailer shown is Midland-built. `competitor` where another manufacturer's branding or a distinctly non-Midland build is visible; `not_a_trailer` for documents, parts and renders with no trailer; `unknown` where there is no evidence either way -- which is the honest answer for most unbranded trailers and must not be guessed.

position_in_frame.description: Which unit this is, so the tags can be matched back to what a viewer sees. Ordered from the prime mover backwards where a combination is coupled.

identifying_text.description: Text legible ON THIS UNIT. Identity signals are the VIN plate and any chassis-marked job or build number -- these are permanent and unit-specific. A REGISTRATION PLATE IS NOT AN IDENTITY SIGNAL: Midland uses trade plates, which move between units, so the same plate across two frames does not mean the same trailer and very often means a different one. Transcribe a plate if legible, but never use it to assert which unit this is, and never use it to link frames.

plate_type.description: Where a plate is legible. `trade_plate` is Midland's own transferable plate, which indicates an unregistered unit being moved or photographed -- typically a new build pre-delivery. It says something about the trailer's STATE, never its identity.

components_visible.description: Parts of THIS unit actually visible in the frame. POSITIVE ONLY -- list what you can see and omit everything else; an empty array means no part of this unit is identifiable. Never list a part because the trailer must have one. This is what makes a photo findable by what it shows: 'a frame with the kingpin in it' is a real request, 'a frame where the kingpin is not visible' is not.

features_present.description: Equipment and options VISIBLY fitted to this unit, using Midland's own job-card accessory vocabulary. POSITIVE ONLY. Only record a feature you can actually see -- do not infer a toolbox from the product category, and do not infer one from the job card. A hallucinated feature is worse than no tag: it will be found by a search and shown to a customer as what they are buying. Use `none_visible` only when the unit is clearly in frame and carries no listed equipment.

combination_role.description: This unit's role in the combination. DELIBERATELY AVOIDS 'a_trailer'/'b_trailer', which have three live readings: coupling type (engineers: A = drawbar-coupled, so a B-double contains NO A-trailer), position (Midland's published position: A = lead, B = rear), and Midland's looser use of 'B trailer' for either unit of a set. 'A trailer'/'B trailer' are search aliases only. lead_trailer is NOT unique -- a B-triple has two lead trailers.

suspension_type.description: Air bag: a rubber bellows between trailing arm and chassis rail, plus air lines and a levelling valve. Spring: a stack of curved steel leaves U-bolted to the axle with eyes and shackles at each end. Visible only when the axle group is in frame and not hidden by mudguards or a low angle -- not_visible is a common and correct answer. Midland advertise the choice on nearly every model.

deck_material.description: SURFACE FINISH ONLY, never a brand. Bisalloy (Australian) and Hardox (Swedish) are both smooth quenched-and-tempered wear plate and are VISUALLY IDENTICAL -- a tag naming either is invented specification. Use smooth_wear_plate. checker_plate is the raised repeating pattern (Midland spell it both checker and chequer). none_skeletal is frame rails with no continuous deck. Timber is NOT a value: no Midland source for timber decking was found. Plate THICKNESS is not visible either.

container_capability.description: What the twist lock positions show the trailer CAN carry -- never what it is rated or plated for. Read best on an EMPTY skel side-on: 4 locks at the extremes = 40ft only; locks at both 20ft and 40ft intervals = 1x40ft or 2x20ft. 45ft generally needs a retractable or extendable chassis. On a loaded trailer, read the container instead.

axle_group_layout.description: Where the axle groups sit along the unit -- an OBSERVATION, not a configuration call. group_each_end and single_group_centre are the ATA's dog and pig geometry. split_group is Midland's Split Axle Group: one axle separated from the rest by 2.5m or more, which is large and unmistakable side-on. Record what you see; let trailer_configuration follow from it.

manufacturer_decal_text.description: Builder's name as ACTUALLY READ from a decal or plate, usually on the headboard or chassis rail near the front. Transcribe only; never infer a manufacturer from livery. Trailer liveries belong to the OPERATOR, not the builder -- a competitor's trailer runs in its owner's colours. Brand-specific product names count as decals: 'Kurtainer' is Krueger's, 'Super Tilt' and 'AZMEB' are FWR's, 'Moving Floor' is Barker's.

manufacturer_confidence.description: How the manufacturer was established. Default unknown. Only ever pair is_midland_product=midland with decal_legible or provenance_only. An unknown-manufacturer tag that blocks publication is cheap; a wrong 'midland' tag on a competitor's trailer is the costly failure this project exists to avoid.

content_purpose.description: What this image was taken FOR. The media library holds more than marketing, and the folder it sits in does not reliably say which - condition and warranty shots are filed alongside product photography. Set `non_marketing` whenever the frame is evidently not marketing-worthy material: damage, wear, rust, defect documentation, weighbridge or compliance records, or an incidental record shot.

non_marketing_reason.description: Required when content_purpose is non_marketing or a record type: one clause on what makes it unsuitable, so a human can overrule it.

competitor_branding_present.description: Whether another manufacturer's branding is anywhere in the frame, including behind or beside a Midland unit. Separate from each trailer's is_midland_product, because the subject can be Midland's while a competitor's trailer sits in the background - which is how it gets published by accident.

competitor_names.description: Manufacturer names actually legible, e.g. "Krueger". Do not guess a make from a silhouette.

duplicate_group.description: Shared id across near-identical frames of one framing, so the best of a burst surfaces and the rest stay findable.

demonstrates.description: What this FRAME is evidence of -- the answer to 'why would anyone pull this photo out of the library'. This is the most search-relevant field in the schema and the only one that describes the photograph's purpose rather than the trailer's specification. A close side view of a control panel demonstrates `twist_lock_system` even though the trailer is a skel and the folder already said so. Use `nothing_specific` for a frame that records a trailer without showing anything in particular.

combination_type.description: The whole combination in frame. Replaces the old single 'road_train_combination' bucket. VISUAL TEST: two bodies close-coupled with the rear one's nose resting on the tail of the one in front, no drawbar and no gap = B-DOUBLE. A drawbar and a visible gap with an axle group under the gap = A-DOUBLE or road train, and that group belongs to the CONVERTER DOLLY, not to either trailer. Drawbar and gap with the front group steering on a turntable = DOG. Use not_a_combination for a single trailer.

ata_configuration_code.description: Optional ATA notation, e.g. B1233 (B-double: single steer, tandem drive, tri lead, tri rear) or A123T23 (Type 1 road train). R = rigid, A = prime mover + semi, T = drawbar or dolly trailer, B = trailer coupled via a turntable on the forward trailer; digits are axles per group. Every symbol is countable from a side-on photograph, and a partial code is fine when only part of the combination is in frame. Null when you cannot count the groups.

audit.description: Computed after tagging, by comparing vision against path_derived. Disagreement is the signal worth acting on: either the frame is filed in the wrong folder, or the tagger is wrong. Both are worth knowing and neither is detectable from one source alone.

provenance_conflict.description: True where path_derived.content_expectation is `competitor` but vision says `midland`, or the reverse. Always route these to human review.

non_marketing_in_marketing_folder.description: True where content_purpose is not marketing_photography but the folder implied it was. The single most useful audit signal found in the first folder test.

$comment: v4. Two conventions that govern every field. (1) not_visible vs unknown are NOT interchangeable: not_visible means the answer exists but the camera did not capture it -- occluded, cropped, or outside the frame; unknown means the subject IS in frame and you genuinely cannot judge it. Keeping them distinct is what lets someone find the photos worth re-shooting. (2) Positive-only array fields (components_visible, features_present, demonstrates, manufacturer_decal_text) list what IS there and omit everything else; an empty array is a valid answer and always beats a guess.

x_input_aliases.description: Strings that appear in the existing 40,000 filenames and folder names. Map to the canonical value ON INPUT ONLY. None of these may ever be emitted as a tag value.
x_input_aliases.note: The two-axle alias is the important one operationally. Midland's OWN website serves image files named for the deprecated term alongside 'Tri+Axle+...' files on the same page, so it is very likely present in the photo library's filenames and folder names. Read it, map it to tandem, never write it.
